subject.title: Feature Request: Automated Session Memory Preservation & Synthesis

question: Should OpenClaw core own structured reset/startup memory synthesis and transcript anchoring, or should core only expose lifecycle/plugin APIs while memory plugins or MCP packages own the synthesis policy?
rationale: The remaining work crosses silent model calls, transcript retention, startup prompt injection, plugin API boundaries, and security policy, so code inspection alone cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Define a bounded core contract
options.body: Make any core behavior explicit and opt-in, with redaction, retention, timeout, dedupe, audit, startup limits, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Route synthesis outside core
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core lean and ask memory plugins or MCP packages such as the linked world-model MCP to own synthesis, adding only missing generic lifecycle APIs if needed.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608 own reset-time agentic flush and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/15828 own extra triggers/summaries, then decide whether this issue remains an umbrella.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Make any core behavior explicit and opt-in, with redaction, retention, timeout, dedupe, audit, startup limits, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The core/plugin memory boundary and internal hook architecture are the main product decision points, and this history points most strongly to steipete for that choice.
